label: neiso 48 ct floor
definition: KEEPER (promoted 2026-07-05, replacing neiso-47): the neiso-47 fast-start keeper recipe on current main with ONE structural change — the two all-24h CT_PEAKER temperature (tmax) reliability-floor limbs (Boston, Connecticut) SCRUBBED (enabled False in reliability_floor_coeffs_NEISO.csv), a zero-parameter mechanism deletion mirroring the caiso-52 CT scrub and the pjm-77 reconcile. Root cause (rules 17/18): the limbs carried no sub-daily window, so on any design-cooling day they forced fast-start CTs at min-stable for ALL 24 h; A/B vs the same-recipe control (neiso-48-base-control, bundle neiso_ctbase) shows D-4 off-window binding 72-76% -> floor removed, C8 CT_PEAKER forced-energy share 0.47/0.78/0.47 -> 0.00 all years, C7 off-peak CV ratio 0.65/0.63/0.59 -> 0.76/0.86/0.79. Disclosed cost (rule #1, NOT to be won back with a floor): CT_PEAKER grid volume falls to 0.010/0.021/0.099 TWh, absorbed by marginal CC_REGULAR at essentially the same price (dw-LMP +$0.02-0.06); every other class moves <0.0012 TWh. Remaining open C7 gate is ST_GAS diurnal shape (pre-existing in neiso-47, unchanged here) — the next NEISO root cause. Still NOT-YET. Promoted as the most structurally faithful NEISO run (rules #1/#12): one confirmed flat-floor bug removed, nothing tuned.
market_story: ISO-NE fast-start peakers are economically dispatched for the afternoon/evening peak, not day-ahead committed at a floor: on hot days the real Boston/Connecticut CT fleet is near-zero overnight. The scrubbed all-24h limbs were forcing roughly half of the (tiny) CT_PEAKER class energy at binding floors and flattening its off-peak profile; removing them restores the spiky peaker signature while the marginal CC block absorbs the ~0.07-0.12 TWh/yr at the same clearing price.
